answer.answer: The study met its goal. Repeats confirmed five challenging settings, each on a different scene: 18f8dbd6 at 1.4x / +2 s (S15), 0e002edd at 1.4x / −2 s (S9), 1bbe02fc at 0.8x / +1.5 s (S16), 07981e6a at 1.2x / −1 s (S3) and 0d4893f5 at 1.4x / +1.5 s (S7). Every kept run at these settings failed. Still, each has only three or four repeats, so the low end of each 90% range sits just above 0.5 and the true rates are only loosely pinned down. In none of the triaged failures did the ego hit the pedestrian. At every confirmed setting the policy drifted left (or, at S9, turned wide) away from the recorded path, then struck a parked or neighbouring vehicle or left the road. So these cases show the policy failing on lane keeping in pedestrian scenes, not on pedestrian crossings, and the pedestrian's step-out time does not appear to drive them. The S9 case also rests entirely on runs flagged as possible simulator artifacts, because the ego ended more than 3.5 m off the recorded path. Triage still blames the policy for them.

findings.claim: In 18f8dbd6 at 1.4x / +2 s every kept run failed: at about 12 m/s the ego drifted left into the next lane and hit the slower car (actor 2) there, without braking. The pedestrian was not involved.
In 0d4893f5 at 1.4x / +1.5 s every kept run failed the same way: going straight through the intersection at about 9 m/s, the ego drifted about 1.5–1.7 m left and sideswiped vehicle 33 alongside it.
In 07981e6a at 1.2x / −1 s every kept run failed: the ego drifted left into the parking lane and hit parked car 6 at 10–12 m/s, barely braking, even though the route called for a right turn.

In 1bbe02fc at 0.8x / +1.5 s every kept run left the road: the policy steered left at an intersection where the route turned right, with no traffic close by. This is the only confirmed case at a reduced speed.

In 0e002edd at 1.4x / −2 s every kept run failed. At about 3 m/s at the intersection, the ego hit crossing or turning vehicles (12, 112) or ran into the curb lane. Every one of these failures is flagged as a possible artifact (ego more than 3.5 m off the recorded path), so this case is the least certain of the five. One run was re-run and only the re-run was kept.

In every triaged failure the policy was at fault, the struck object was a vehicle (or the ego left the road), and the retimed pedestrian was never hit. This fits the left drift noted in the brief, which persists at 2 Hz.
Step-out time shows no consistent direction across the confirmed cases: they range from 2 s earlier to 2 s later. High ego speed (1.2x–1.4x) is common to four of the five.

Two scenes failed only some of the time. In 048b974e at 1.2x / +1.5 s the ego bent left into parked car 68; in 18d28973 at 1.4x / +1 s it did not brake for a nearly stopped car ahead. Their ranges span 0.5 on both sides, so neither scene is confirmed, nor ruled out.
The settings tried on 12a09194 and 0b10bce8, and some other settings on the remaining scenes, produced no failures. Each was tried only once or twice, so that is a hint, not evidence of safety.

open: No run was made at the nominal setting (1.0x, 0 s) on any confirmed scene. So it is unknown whether these scenes fail anyway because of the left drift, rather than because of the speed–timing combination. A few repeats at 1.0x / 0 s on 18f8dbd6, 0d4893f5, 07981e6a, 1bbe02fc and 0e002edd would settle it.

No setting produced a pedestrian collision, so the study does not answer which speed/timing combinations make the policy hit the pedestrian. A follow-up could search near the pedestrian's conflict point, and record closest approach to the pedestrian rather than to any actor.

The 0e002edd case (S9) rests on failures where the ego was far off the recorded path, so rendering could explain them. Video review focused on the rendering, or repeats at a setting that keeps the ego closer to the recorded path, would separate rendering effects from policy behaviour.
The confirmed cases have only three or four repeats each. A few more repeats per setting would narrow the ranges well above 0.5.
048b974e (S1) and 18d28973 (S12) are unresolved: more repeats there, or nearby settings, would show whether they belong in the top cases.
The comparison with the 10 Hz study pedestrian_ego_speed is not in these results. Running the same five settings at 10 Hz would show whether 2 Hz planning changes them.
